agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — the codebase currently has no preview-mode awareness. The central attachment point is useContent (236+ callers), which all Contentstack components delegate to. The change should plug into the hook/provider layer so that every downstream component automatically serves draft content when the app is in preview mode, without modifying individual components. Contentstack APIs are unreachable at test time, so VCs are framed to our side of the boundary.

Openspec provided an empty acceptance criteria list with architectural guidance that the change should plug into the useContent hook/provider layer so all downstream components automatically serve draft content in preview mode. I built the full AC set from scratch based on that guidance and the story context. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 ensures backward compatibility — non-preview behavior is unchanged. (2) AC-2 establishes the core preview behavior. (3) AC-3 and AC-4 cover preview mode lifecycle — persistence across routes and clean exit. (4) AC-5 addresses error handling for API failures during preview. (5) AC-6 ensures all Contentstack component types (links, images, cards) are covered, not just text. (6) AC-7 requires a visible preview indicator for UX clarity. (7) AC-8 adds a security gate — preview should not be activatable in production. (8) AC-9 addresses the 'live' aspect — draft updates should reflect without full reload. (9) AC-10 covers nested/reference content resolution. (10) AC-11 prevents stale content flash during loading. (11) AC-12 ensures URL shareability of preview mode. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual file contents (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, etc.), so these ACs are based solely on the story title, description, and file paths. A human should verify these align with the actual codebase architecture, particularly the Contentstack Live Preview SDK integration pattern and any existing preview-related code.
